1. Which of the following expresses the ratio $\frac{\text{mass of a proton}}{\text{mass of a electron}}$ as a difference in orders of magnitude?
A. $-3$
B. 0
C. 3
D. 6

2.text_clean:
2. A body moves in a straight line. In order for the equations for uniformly accelerated motion to be applied, which condition must be true?
A. A constant net force acts on the body of fixed mass.
B. A constant net force acts on the body.
C. The body falls towards the surface of a planet.
D. The body has an initial velocity of zero.

3.text_clean:
3. The graph shows the variation with time of the velocity of a truck of fixed mass.
[Graph: velocity against time; velocity starts positive, decreases with decreasing gradient, crosses zero with small but non-zero gradient, then becomes increasingly negative; time t marked by a dashed line]
What can be deduced from the graph?
A. The truck is always accelerating.
B. The truck is always moving.
C. The truck is always moving in one direction.
D. The displacement of the truck after time t is zero.

4.text_clean:
4. A girl is standing on a moving skateboard. She pushes backwards on the ground at intervals as shown on the graph.
[Graph: force / N (0-90) against distance / m (0-50); three triangular pulses of peak 80 N, each 5 m wide, at 5-10 m, 25-30 m and 40-45 m]
How much kinetic energy is gained by the girl during the period represented on the graph? Frictional forces are negligible.
A. 200 J
B. 400 J
C. 600 J
D. 1200 J

5.text_clean:
5. An electron moves with uniform circular motion in a region of magnetic field. Which diagram shows the acceleration a and velocity v of the electron at point P?
[Diagrams: four circles with point P at the top.
A. v and a both pointing down (towards centre)
B. v pointing left (tangential), a pointing down (towards centre)
C. a pointing left (tangential), v pointing down (towards centre)
D. v and a both pointing left (tangential)]

6. Equal masses of water at 80 °C and paraffin at 20 °C are mixed in a container of negligible thermal capacity. The specific heat capacity of water is twice that of paraffin. What is the final temperature of the mixture?
A. 30 °C
B. 40 °C
C. 50 °C
D. 60 °C

A. The gas is at high pressure.
B. There are weak forces of attraction between the particles in the gas.
C. The collisions between the particles are elastic.
D. The energy of the particles is proportional to the absolute temperature.

Change in internal energy | Work done
A. 0 | greater than W
B. 0 | less than W
C. greater than 0 | less than W
D. less than 0 | same as W

A. molecules in the block has decreased.
B. surroundings has increased.
C. universe has increased.
D. universe has decreased.

A. straight line decreasing from positive through zero to negative
B. U-shaped curve touching zero
C. sinusoid of constant amplitude
D. sinusoid of decreasing amplitude (damped)]

A. 250 Hz
B. 500 Hz
C. 1000 Hz
D. 2000 Hz

A. A sound of constant frequency but varying in amplitude
B. A sound of constantly varying frequency
C. A sound with a frequency of 50 Hz
D. A sound with a frequency of 200 Hz

A. Replacing the narrow slit with a circular aperture of same size.
B. Moving the two sources further from the aperture.
C. Using red light.
D. Using violet light.
